import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.WeightedSupport
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.NilpotentDefect

/-!
# Canonical truncation before substitution

Polynomials are represented with U outermost, Z in the middle, and the X variables
innermost.  Truncation is an operation on canonical polynomial representatives;
we never assert that U = 1 defines a map out of the truncated quotient.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.Truncation

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators

variable {R ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R]

abbrev Poly (ι R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] :=
  Polynomial (Polynomial (MvPolynomial ι R))

/-- Delete all coefficients of degree at least n. -/
def trunc {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (n : ℕ) (P : Polynomial A) : Polynomial A :=
  Polynomial.ofFinsupp (.ofCoeff (P.toFinsupp.coeff.filter fun j => j < n))

@[simp] theorem coeff_trunc {A : Type*} [Semiring A]
    (n j : ℕ) (P : Polynomial A) :
    (trunc n P).coeff j = if j < n then P.coeff j else 0 := by
  classical
  simp [trunc, Polynomial.coeff, Finsupp.filter_apply]

@[simp] theorem trunc_zero {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (n : ℕ) :
    trunc n (0 : Polynomial A) = 0 := by
  ext j
  simp

@[simp] theorem trunc_add {A : Type*} [Semiring A]
    (n : ℕ) (P Q : Polynomial A) :
    trunc n (P + Q) = trunc n P + trunc n Q := by
  ext j
  by_cases h : j < n <;> simp [h]

/-- Delete X monomials whose total degree exceeds N. -/
def xTrunc (N : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial ι R) : MvPolynomial ι R :=
  .ofCoeff ((AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff P).filter
    fun a : ι →₀ ℕ => a.sum (fun _ k => k) ≤ N)

@[simp] theorem coeff_xTrunc (N : ℕ) (a : ι →₀ ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial ι R) :
    (xTrunc N P).coeff a =
      if a.sum (fun _ k => k) ≤ N then P.coeff a else 0 := by
  classical
  simp [xTrunc, Finsupp.filter_apply]

@[simp] theorem xTrunc_zero (N : ℕ) : xTrunc N (0 : MvPolynomial ι R) = 0 := by
  ext a
  simp

import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.LeanCompat
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Incidence
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Types

namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-!
# Incidence slots and globally consistent factor words

Section 5.4 assigns each coordinate's incident factors to different slots.
The same factor word is then used at every incidence of that factor.  The
slot numbers themselves need not agree at different coordinates.

The ordered constructor and the slot-filling operations are computable.  An
additional constructor for arbitrary finite factor types chooses an enumeration.
No running-time bound or probabilistic independence assertion is hidden here.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.SlotAssignment

open SubexponentialSAT.Factor SubexponentialSAT.Types

variable {V E : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- The actual factors incident to one coordinate. -/
abbrev Incident (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) := {e : E // v ∈ P.scope e}

/-- An injective slot assignment separately at each coordinate. -/
abbrev SlotMap (P : Pattern V E) (Δ : ℕ) :=
  (v : V) → Incident P v ↪ Fin Δ

@[simp] theorem card_incident [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) :
    Fintype.card (Incident P v) =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun e => v ∈ P.scope e).card := by
  exact Fintype.card_subtype _

/-- The incidence bound supplies exactly the cardinal inequality needed for slots. -/
theorem card_incident_le [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) (v : V) : Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ := by
  rw [card_incident]
  exact hP.incidence_le v

/-- A finite slot assignment, using a chosen enumeration for each incident set. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.equivFin (Incident P v)).toEmbedding.trans (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Slot assignments exist for every bounded factor pattern. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfBounded [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  slotsOfCardLE P (card_incident_le P hP)

/-- For ordered factor indices, sort the incident factors and use their ranks.
This constructor makes the fixed local ordering in the exposition explicit. -/
def orderedSlotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] [LinearOrder E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.orderIsoFinOfCardEq (Incident P v) rfl).symm.toEquiv.toEmbedding.trans
    (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Computable slot assignment for a bounded pattern with ordered factor indices. -/

import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Incidence
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Types

namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-!
# Incidence slots and globally consistent factor words

Section 5.4 assigns each coordinate's incident factors to different slots.
The same factor word is then used at every incidence of that factor.  The
slot numbers themselves need not agree at different coordinates.

The ordered constructor and the slot-filling operations are computable.  An
additional constructor for arbitrary finite factor types chooses an enumeration.
No running-time bound or probabilistic independence assertion is hidden here.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.SlotAssignment

open SubexponentialSAT.Factor SubexponentialSAT.Types

variable {V E : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- The actual factors incident to one coordinate. -/
abbrev Incident (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) := {e : E // v ∈ P.scope e}

/-- An injective slot assignment separately at each coordinate. -/
abbrev SlotMap (P : Pattern V E) (Δ : ℕ) :=
  (v : V) → Incident P v ↪ Fin Δ

@[simp] theorem card_incident [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) :
    Fintype.card (Incident P v) =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun e => v ∈ P.scope e).card := by
  exact Fintype.card_subtype _

/-- The incidence bound supplies exactly the cardinal inequality needed for slots. -/
theorem card_incident_le [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) (v : V) : Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ := by
  rw [card_incident]
  exact hP.incidence_le v

/-- A finite slot assignment, using a chosen enumeration for each incident set. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.equivFin (Incident P v)).toEmbedding.trans (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Slot assignments exist for every bounded factor pattern. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfBounded [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  slotsOfCardLE P (card_incident_le P hP)

/-- For ordered factor indices, sort the incident factors and use their ranks.
This constructor makes the fixed local ordering in the exposition explicit. -/
def orderedSlotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] [LinearOrder E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.orderIsoFinOfCardEq (Incident P v) rfl).symm.toEquiv.toEmbedding.trans
    (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Computable slot assignment for a bounded pattern with ordered factor indices. -/

# MODULE: q2_block_codebook
SOURCES: include/strata/artifact/dequant.hpp, tools/gguf_writer.py, tools/canonical_xcheck.py
Integer-level model of the Q2_0 block (64 elements, fp16 scale, 16 bytes of 2-bit codes): code
extraction, the asymmetric codebook {-1,0,+1,+2}, the LSB-first byte/bit addressing, the writer's
quantizer, and the requantization fixed-point property used as the writer's self-check.

## Source semantics
* block = { fp16 d; uint8 qs[16] }, 64 elements, 18 bytes.
* element j lives in byte j/4 at bit offset (j%4)*2; code = (qs[j/4] >> (j%4)*2) & 3.
* value = (code - 1) * d; the `- 1` is an integer bias applied before the multiply.
* the writer picks d = amax and code = clamp(round(w/d) + 1, 0, 3); since |w| ≤ d the rounded
  symbol is in {-1,0,1}, so the writer never emits code 3.
* requantizing dequantized values reproduces the codes exactly, PROVIDED no code is 3 and at least
  one code is non-1 (otherwise amax changes). Code 3 breaks the fixed point.

## Form template identifiers
dequantize_q2_0 / dequantize_row_q2_0 / from_s2 → `q2Value`; qs byte addressing → `q2ByteIndex`,
`q2BitOffset`; code extraction → `q2Code`; quantize_q2_0 clamp → `q2Quantize`; to_s2 unpack
`codes[:, t::4]` → `q2Code` with j = 4*b + t; QK=64, BLOCK_BYTES=18 → `qk`, `blockBytes`.
-/

namespace Strata.Q2Block

-- § constants

/-- Elements per Q2_0 block. -/
def qk : Nat := 64
/-- Bytes per Q2_0 block: a 2-byte fp16 scale plus 16 code bytes. -/
def blockBytes : Nat := 18

/-- The block size is exactly the fp16 scale plus 2 bits per element. -/
theorem blockBytes_eq : blockBytes = 2 + qk * 2 / 8 := by decide

-- § addressing

/-- Byte holding element `j` (`j / 4`). -/
def q2ByteIndex (j : Nat) : Nat := j / 4
/-- Bit offset of element `j` inside its byte (`(j % 4) * 2`). -/
def q2BitOffset (j : Nat) : Nat := (j % 4) * 2

/-- Every element of a block addresses one of the 16 code bytes. -/
theorem byteIndex_lt (j : Nat) (hj : j < qk) : q2ByteIndex j < 16 := by
  unfold q2ByteIndex qk at *; omega

/-- Bit offsets are 0, 2, 4 or 6, so a 2-bit field never crosses a byte. -/
theorem bitOffset_le (j : Nat) : q2BitOffset j ≤ 6 := by
  unfold q2BitOffset; omega

/-- Addressing is injective: distinct elements use distinct (byte, bit) slots. -/
theorem address_injective (i j : Nat)
    (hb : q2ByteIndex i = q2ByteIndex j) (ho : q2BitOffset i = q2BitOffset j) : i = j := by
  unfold q2ByteIndex q2BitOffset at *; omega

/-- `to_s2`'s slice `codes[:, t::4]` for byte `b` is element `4*b + t`: the same addressing. -/
theorem slice_matches_address (b t : Nat) (ht : t < 4) :
    q2ByteIndex (4 * b + t) = b ∧ q2BitOffset (4 * b + t) = 2 * t := by
  unfold q2ByteIndex q2BitOffset; omega

-- § codes and values

/-- The 2-bit code of element `j` read from byte `byte`. -/
def q2Code (byte j : Nat) : Nat := (byte >>> q2BitOffset j) &&& 3

/-- Extracted codes are always in `0..3`. -/
theorem q2Code_lt (byte j : Nat) : q2Code byte j < 4 := by
  have h : q2Code byte j = (byte >>> q2BitOffset j) % 2 ^ 2 := by
    unfold q2Code
    exact Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod _ 2
  rw [h]; exact Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)

/-- The integer symbol of a code: `code - 1`. -/
def q2Symbol (c : Nat) : Int := (c : Int) - 1

/-- Dequantized value in units of an integer scale `d`. -/
def q2Value (c : Nat) (d : Int) : Int := q2Symbol c * d

/-- The codebook is asymmetric: the four symbols are exactly -1, 0, +1, +2. -/
theorem symbol_set (c : Nat) (hc : c < 4) :
    q2Symbol c = -1 ∨ q2Symbol c = 0 ∨ q2Symbol c = 1 ∨ q2Symbol c = 2 := by
  unfold q2Symbol; omega

/-- Structural invariant of `--check`: every value is one of `-d, 0, d, 2d`. -/
theorem value_set (byte j : Nat) (d : Int) :
    let v := q2Value (q2Code byte j) d
    v = -d ∨ v = 0 ∨ v = d ∨ v = 2 * d := by
  have hc := q2Code_lt byte j
  have hs := symbol_set (q2Code byte j) hc
  simp only [q2Value]
  rcases hs with h | h | h | h <;> rw [h] <;> omega

/-- Decoding unsigned codes as `code * d` (no bias) is wrong on every element. -/
theorem unbiased_decode_differs (c : Nat) (d : Int) (hd : d ≠ 0) :
    q2Value c d ≠ (c : Int) * d := by
  unfold q2Value q2Symbol
  intro h
  have : ((c : Int) - 1) * d - (c : Int) * d = 0 := by omega
  have : -d = 0 := by
    have e : ((c : Int) - 1) * d - (c : Int) * d = -d := by
      rw [Int.sub_mul, Int.one_mul]; omega
    omega
  omega

-- § quantizer

/-- `clamp(r + 1, 0, 3)` applied to an integer rounded symbol `r`. -/
def q2Quantize (r : Int) : Nat := (max 0 (min 3 (r + 1))).toNat

/-- The quantizer always yields a valid 2-bit code. -/
theorem q2Quantize_lt (r : Int) : q2Quantize r < 4 := by
  unfold q2Quantize; omega

/-- With `d = amax`, the rounded symbol lies in `[-1, 1]`, so the writer never emits code 3. -/
theorem quantize_never_three (r : Int) (h1 : -1 ≤ r) (h2 : r ≤ 1) : q2Quantize r ≤ 2 := by
  unfold q2Quantize; omega

/-- On symbols the codebook can represent, quantization inverts `q2Symbol`. -/
theorem quantize_symbol (c : Nat) (hc : c < 4) : q2Quantize (q2Symbol c) = c := by
  unfold q2Quantize q2Symbol; omega

-- § requantization fixed point

/-- Exact division recovers the symbol from a dequantized value. -/
theorem value_div_scale (c : Nat) (d : Int) (hd : d ≠ 0) : q2Value c d / d = q2Symbol c := by

extraction, the asymmetric codebook {-1,0,+1,+2}, the LSB-first byte/bit addressing, the writer's
quantizer, and the requantization fixed-point property used as the writer's self-check.

* block = { fp16 d; uint8 qs[16] }, 64 elements, 18 bytes.
* element j lives in byte j/4 at bit offset (j%4)*2; code = (qs[j/4] >> (j%4)*2) & 3.
* value = (code - 1) * d; the `- 1` is an integer bias applied before the multiply.
* the writer picks d = amax and code = clamp(round(w/d) + 1, 0, 3); since |w| ≤ d the rounded
  symbol is in {-1,0,1}, so the writer never emits code 3.
* requantizing dequantized values reproduces the codes exactly, PROVIDED no code is 3 and at least
  one code is non-1 (otherwise amax changes). Code 3 breaks the fixed point.

## Form template identifiers
dequantize_q2_0 / dequantize_row_q2_0 / from_s2 → `q2Value`; qs byte addressing → `q2ByteIndex`,
`q2BitOffset`; code extraction → `q2Code`; quantize_q2_0 clamp → `q2Quantize`; to_s2 unpack
`codes[:, t::4]` → `q2Code` with j = 4*b + t; QK=64, BLOCK_BYTES=18 → `qk`, `blockBytes`.
-/

namespace Strata.Q2Block

-- § constants

/-- Elements per Q2_0 block. -/
def qk : Nat := 64
/-- Bytes per Q2_0 block: a 2-byte fp16 scale plus 16 code bytes. -/
def blockBytes : Nat := 18

/-- The block size is exactly the fp16 scale plus 2 bits per element. -/
theorem blockBytes_eq : blockBytes = 2 + qk * 2 / 8 := by decide

-- § addressing

/-- Byte holding element `j` (`j / 4`). -/
def q2ByteIndex (j : Nat) : Nat := j / 4
/-- Bit offset of element `j` inside its byte (`(j % 4) * 2`). -/
def q2BitOffset (j : Nat) : Nat := (j % 4) * 2

/-- Every element of a block addresses one of the 16 code bytes. -/
theorem byteIndex_lt (j : Nat) (hj : j < qk) : q2ByteIndex j < 16 := by
  unfold q2ByteIndex qk at *; omega

/-- Bit offsets are 0, 2, 4 or 6, so a 2-bit field never crosses a byte. -/
theorem bitOffset_le (j : Nat) : q2BitOffset j ≤ 6 := by
  unfold q2BitOffset; omega

/-- Addressing is injective: distinct elements use distinct (byte, bit) slots. -/
theorem address_injective (i j : Nat)
    (hb : q2ByteIndex i = q2ByteIndex j) (ho : q2BitOffset i = q2BitOffset j) : i = j := by
  unfold q2ByteIndex q2BitOffset at *; omega

/-- `to_s2`'s slice `codes[:, t::4]` for byte `b` is element `4*b + t`: the same addressing. -/
theorem slice_matches_address (b t : Nat) (ht : t < 4) :
    q2ByteIndex (4 * b + t) = b ∧ q2BitOffset (4 * b + t) = 2 * t := by
  unfold q2ByteIndex q2BitOffset; omega

-- § codes and values

/-- The 2-bit code of element `j` read from byte `byte`. -/
def q2Code (byte j : Nat) : Nat := (byte >>> q2BitOffset j) &&& 3

/-- Extracted codes are always in `0..3`. -/
theorem q2Code_lt (byte j : Nat) : q2Code byte j < 4 := by
  have h : q2Code byte j = (byte >>> q2BitOffset j) % 2 ^ 2 := by
    unfold q2Code
    exact Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod _ 2
  rw [h]; exact Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)

/-- Dequantized value in units of an integer scale `d`. -/
def q2Value (c : Nat) (d : Int) : Int := q2Symbol c * d

/-- The codebook is asymmetric: the four symbols are exactly -1, 0, +1, +2. -/
theorem symbol_set (c : Nat) (hc : c < 4) :
    q2Symbol c = -1 ∨ q2Symbol c = 0 ∨ q2Symbol c = 1 ∨ q2Symbol c = 2 := by
  unfold q2Symbol; omega

/-- Structural invariant of `--check`: every value is one of `-d, 0, d, 2d`. -/
theorem value_set (byte j : Nat) (d : Int) :
    let v := q2Value (q2Code byte j) d
    v = -d ∨ v = 0 ∨ v = d ∨ v = 2 * d := by
  have hc := q2Code_lt byte j
  have hs := symbol_set (q2Code byte j) hc
  simp only [q2Value]
  rcases hs with h | h | h | h <;> rw [h] <;> omega

theorem unbiased_decode_differs (c : Nat) (d : Int) (hd : d ≠ 0) :
    q2Value c d ≠ (c : Int) * d := by
  unfold q2Value q2Symbol
  intro h
  have : ((c : Int) - 1) * d - (c : Int) * d = 0 := by omega
  have : -d = 0 := by
    have e : ((c : Int) - 1) * d - (c : Int) * d = -d := by

def normalize (m : Nat) : Nat × Nat := normAux 11 m 0

theorem normAux_spec (f m s : Nat) :
    (normAux f m s).1 = m * 2 ^ ((normAux f m s).2 - s) ∧ s ≤ (normAux f m s).2 := by
  induction f generalizing m s with
  | zero => simp [normAux]
  | succ f ih =>
    unfold normAux
    split
    · simp
    · obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := ih (m * 2) (s + 1)
      refine ⟨?_, by omega⟩
      rw [h1]
      have e : (normAux f (m * 2) (s + 1)).2 - s = ((normAux f (m * 2) (s + 1)).2 - (s + 1)) + 1 := by
        omega
      rw [e, Nat.pow_succ]
      simp [Nat.mul_comm, Nat.mul_left_comm]

  have h := (normAux_spec 11 m 0).1

  set_option maxRecDepth 200000 in decide

  let sign := h / 32768 % 2
  let ex := h / 1024 % 32

    if man = 0 then sign * 2 ^ 31
    else sign * 2 ^ 31 + (113 - (normalize man).2) * 2 ^ 23 + ((normalize man).1 % 1024) * 2 ^ 13

def f16FromF32 (x : Nat) : Nat :=
  let sign := x / 2 ^ 31 * 32768
  let raw := x / 2 ^ 23 % 256
  let man := x % 2 ^ 23
  if raw = 255 then sign + 0x7C00 + (if man ≠ 0 then 0x200 else 0)
  else if 143 ≤ raw then sign + 0x7C00
  else if raw ≤ 112 then
    if raw < 102 then sign
    else
      let m := man + 2 ^ 23
      let sh := 126 - raw
      let h := m / 2 ^ sh % 1024
      let rem := m % 2 ^ sh
      let half := 2 ^ (sh - 1)
      if rem > half ∨ (rem = half ∧ h % 2 = 1) then sign + h + 1 else sign + h

    let h := sign + (raw - 112) * 1024 + man / 2 ^ 13

  let man := x % 2 ^ 23
  if 143 ≤ raw then sign + 0x7C00 + (if man ≠ 0 then 0x200 else 0) else f16FromF32 x

/-- 1.0 narrows to 0x3C00 and 65504 (fp16 max) to 0x7BFF. -/
theorem narrow_one_and_max : f16FromF32 0x3F800000 = 0x3C00 ∧ f16FromF32 0x477FE000 = 0x7BFF := by
  decide

/-- Finite overflow saturates to +inf: 65536.0 and 1e30 both give 0x7C00. -/
theorem narrow_finite_overflow :
    f16FromF32 0x47800000 = 0x7C00 ∧ f16FromF32 0x7149F2CA = 0x7C00 := by decide

/-- Round 198's finding: the conflated test returns a NaN (0x7E00) for the finite value 1e30. -/
theorem conflated_returns_nan : f16FromF32Conflated 0x7149F2CA = 0x7E00 := by decide

    f16FromF32 0x7F800000 = 0x7C00 ∧ f16FromF32 0xFF800000 = 0xFC00 ∧
      f16FromF32 0x7FC00000 = 0x7E00 := by decide

theorem narrow_subnormal :
    f16FromF32 0x33800000 = 0x0001 ∧ f16FromF32 0x33000000 = 0x0000 := by decide

    f32FromF16 0x3C00 = 0x3F800000 ∧ f32FromF16 0x0001 = 0x33800000 ∧

    f16FromF32 (f32FromF16 (s * 32768 + ex * 1024 + man)) = s * 32768 + ex * 1024 + man := by

  have hex : (s * 32768 + ex * 1024 + man) / 1024 % 32 = ex := by omega
  have hman : (s * 32768 + ex * 1024 + man) % 1024 = man := by omega
  have hw : f32FromF16 (s * 32768 + ex * 1024 + man) =

    simp only [f32FromF16, hsign, hex, hman]
    have h0 : ex ≠ 0 := by omega
    have h31 : ex ≠ 31 := by omega
    simp [h0, h31]
  rw [hw]
  simp only [f16FromF32]
  have hr : (s * 2 ^ 31 + (ex + 112) * 2 ^ 23 + man * 2 ^ 13) / 2 ^ 23 % 256 = ex + 112 := by
    omega
  have hsg : (s * 2 ^ 31 + (ex + 112) * 2 ^ 23 + man * 2 ^ 13) / 2 ^ 31 = s := by omega
  have hm2 : (s * 2 ^ 31 + (ex + 112) * 2 ^ 23 + man * 2 ^ 13) % 2 ^ 23 = man * 2 ^ 13 := by

  rw [hr, hsg, hm2]
  have a1 : ex + 112 ≠ 255 := by omega
  have a2 : ¬ 143 ≤ ex + 112 := by omega
  have a3 : ¬ ex + 112 ≤ 112 := by omega
  have a4 : man * 2 ^ 13 / 2 ^ 13 = man := by omega
  have a5 : man * 2 ^ 13 % 2 ^ 13 = 0 := by omega
  simp only [a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, if_false]
  have a6 : ex + 112 - 112 = ex := by omega
  rw [a6]
  have a7 : ¬ (0 > 4096 ∨ (0 = 4096 ∧ (s * 32768 + ex * 1024 + man) % 2 = 1)) := by omega
  simp only [a7, if_false]

  rfl

  unfold f32FromBf16; rw [Nat.shiftLeft_eq]; rfl

  rw [widen_eq]; omega

  unfold bf16FromF32; omega

{"language": "plaintext", "code": "/-!
# MODULE: gguf_header_layout
SOURCES: include/strata/artifact/gguf_reader.hpp, tools/gguf_reader.py, tools/gguf_writer.py
The GGUF v3 header contract shared by the C++ reader, the Python reader and the Python writer:
ggml type ids and block geometry, the magic, data-section alignment, per-tensor byte counts, the
writer's aligned offsets, and the `qwen4exp` architecture guard.

## Source semantics
* magic 0x46554747 is "GGUF" read little-endian; only version 3 is accepted.
* block geometry (elements, bytes) per type; Q2_0 (id 42) is (64, 18). Each byte count equals the
  sum of that block's fields.
* where the C++ table defines a geometry, the Python table agrees with it.
* known table discrepancies: Python names id 41 "Q4_0_8_8" (a duplicate of id 33; C++ says
  "Q1_0"), and the C++ name table has no entry for id 29 (IQ1_M) although its geometry table does.
* data_start = pos rounded up to the alignment (default 32); the writer pads every tensor to the
  alignment, so offsets are aligned and non-overlapping.
* expected_bytes = elements / block_elems * block_bytes when elements is a multiple of block_elems.
* the architecture guard accepts iff general.architecture = "qwen4exp" and six hyperparameters
  equal the compiled constants (48, 2560, 512, 10, 24, 2).

## Form template identifiers
block_geometry → `cppGeometry`; BLOCK_GEOMETRY ∘ GGML_TYPES → `pyGeometry`; ggml_type_name →
`cppTypeName`; GGML_TYPES → `pyTypeName`; data_start rounding / writer padding → `alignUp`;
TensorInfo.expected_bytes → `expectedBytes`; check_architecture → `checkArch`; Qwen4ExpGuard →
`guardReqs`.
-/

namespace Strata.Gguf

-- § type tables

/-- C++ `block_geometry`: (elements per block, bytes per block). -/
def cppGeometry : Nat → Option (Nat × Nat)
  | 0 => some (1, 4) | 1 => some (1, 2) | 30 => some (1, 2)
  | 2 => some (32, 18) | 3 => some (32, 20) | 6 => some (32, 22) | 7 => some (32, 24)
  | 8 => some (32, 34) | 9 => some (32, 36)
  | 10 => some (256, 84) | 11 => some (256, 110) | 12 => some (256, 144)
  | 13 => some (256, 176) | 14 => some (256, 210)
  | 16 => some (256, 66) | 17 => some (256, 74) | 18 => some (256, 98)
  | 20 => some (32, 18) | 21 => some (256, 110) | 22 => some (256, 82) | 23 => some (256, 136)
  | 29 => some (256, 56) | 42 => some (64, 18)
  | _ => none

/-- Python `BLOCK_GEOMETRY` looked up through `GGML_TYPES`, as a function of the type id. -/
def pyGeometry : Nat → Option (Nat × Nat)
  | 0 => some (1, 4) | 1 => some (1, 2) | 30 => some (1, 2) | 28 => some (1, 8)
  | 2 => some (32, 18) | 3 => some (32, 20) | 6 => some (32, 22) | 7 => some (32, 24)
  | 8 => some (32, 34) | 9 => some (32, 36)
  | 10 => some (256, 84) | 11 => some (256, 110) | 12 => some (256, 144)
  | 13 => some (256, 176) | 14 => some (256, 210) | 15 => some (256, 292)
  | 16 => some (256, 66) | 17 => some (256, 74) | 18 => some (256, 98) | 19 => some (256, 50)
  | 20 => some (32, 18) | 21 => some (256, 110) | 22 => some (256, 82) | 23 => some (256, 136)
  | 29 => some (256, 56) | 39 => some (32, 17) | 40 => some (64, 36) | 42 => some (64, 18)
  | _ => none

/-- C++ `ggml_type_name` for the ids where the tables are discussed below. -/
def cppTypeName : Nat → String
  | 29 => "?" | 33 => "?" | 41 => "Q1_0" | 42 => "Q2_0" | _ => "other"

/-- Python `GGML_TYPES` for the same ids. -/
def pyTypeName : Nat → String
  | 29 => "IQ1_M" | 33 => "Q4_0_8_8" | 41 => "Q4_0_8_8" | 42 => "Q2_0" | _ => "other"

-- § geometry facts

/-- Q2_0 is 64 elements in 18 bytes in both readers. -/
theorem q2_0_geometry : cppGeometry 42 = some (64, 18) ∧ pyGeometry 42 = some (64, 18) := by
  decide

/-- Wherever the C++ reader defines a geometry, the Python reference agrees (ids 0..63). -/
theorem cpp_geometry_agrees_with_py :
    (List.range 64).all (fun t => (cppGeometry t).isNone || cppGeometry t == pyGeometry t) = true := by
  decide

/-- Every byte count is the sum of the block's fields, as laid out in the dequantizers. -/
theorem geometry_field_sums :
    cppGeometry 2 = some (32, 2 + 16) ∧            -- Q4_0: d, qs[16]
    cppGeometry 6 = some (32, 2 + 4 + 16) ∧        -- Q5_0: d, qh[4], qs[16]
    cppGeometry 8 = some (32, 2 + 32) ∧            -- Q8_0: d, qs[32]
    cppGeometry 11 = some (256, 32 + 64 + 12 + 2) ∧ -- Q3_K: hmask, qs, scales, d
    cppGeometry 12 = some (256, 2 + 2 + 12 + 128) ∧ -- Q4_K: d, dmin, scales, qs
    cppGeometry 13 = some (256, 2 + 2 + 12 + 32 + 128) ∧ -- Q5_K: d, dmin, scales, qh, qs
    cppGeometry 14 = some (256, 128 + 64 + 16 + 2) ∧ -- Q6_K: ql, qh, scales, d
    cppGeometry 20 = some (32, 2 + 16) ∧           -- IQ4_NL: d, qs[16]
    cppGeometry 23 = some (256, 2 + 2 + 4 + 128) ∧  -- IQ4_XS: d, scales_h, scales_l, qs
    cppGeometry 42 = some (64, 2 + 16) := by        -- Q2_0: d, qs[16]
  decide

/-- Table discrepancy: Python names id 41 like id 33, and C++ names it Q1_0. -/
theorem py_name_41_duplicate : pyTypeName 41 = pyTypeName 33 ∧ cppTypeName 41 ≠ pyTypeName 41 := by
  decide

/-- Table discrepancy: C++ has a geometry for id 29 but no name for it. -/
theorem cpp_iq1m_unnamed : (cppGeometry 29).isSome = true ∧ cppTypeName 29 = "?" := by
  decide

-- § magic

/-- The magic constant is the four bytes 'G','G','U','F' read little-endian. -/
theorem magic_bytes : 0x46554747 = 0x47 + 0x47 * 256 + 0x55 * 65536 + 0x46 * 16777216 := by decide

-- § alignment

/-- Round `n` up to a multiple of `a`, as `(n + a - 1) / a * a`. -/
def alignUp (n a : Nat) : Nat := (n + a - 1) / a * a

/-- The rounded value is a multiple of the alignment. -/
theorem alignUp_dvd (n a : Nat) : (alignUp n a) % a = 0 := by
  unfold alignUp; exact Nat.mul_mod_left _ _

/-- Rounding up never moves backwards. -/
theorem alignUp_ge (n a : Nat) (ha : 0 < a) : n ≤ alignUp n a := by
  unfold alignUp
  have h := Nat.div_add_mod (n + a - 1) a
  have hm := Nat.mod_lt (n + a - 1) ha
  have : (n + a - 1) / a * a = a * ((n + a - 1) / a) := Nat.mul_comm _ _
  omega

/-- Rounding up moves forward by less than one alignment step. -/
theorem alignUp_lt (n a : Nat) (ha : 0 < a) : alignUp n a < n + a := by
  unfold alignUp
  have h := Nat.div_add_mod (n + a - 1) a
  have : (n + a - 1) / a * a = a * ((n + a - 1) / a) := Nat.mul_comm _ _
  omega

/-- The writer's padding `(-len) % align` reaches the same aligned position as `alignUp`. -/
theorem writer_pad_eq (n : Nat) : n + (32 - n % 32) % 32 = alignUp n 32 := by

SOURCES: include/strata/artifact/gguf_reader.hpp, tools/gguf_reader.py, tools/gguf_writer.py

ggml type ids and block geometry, the magic, data-section alignment, per-tensor byte counts, the
writer's aligned offsets, and the `qwen4exp` architecture guard.

## Source semantics
* magic 0x46554747 is "GGUF" read little-endian; only version 3 is accepted.
* block geometry (elements, bytes) per type; Q2_0 (id 42) is (64, 18). Each byte count equals the
  sum of that block's fields.
* where the C++ table defines a geometry, the Python table agrees with it.
* known table discrepancies: Python names id 41 "Q4_0_8_8" (a duplicate of id 33; C++ says
  "Q1_0"), and the C++ name table has no entry for id 29 (IQ1_M) although its geometry table does.
* data_start = pos rounded up to the alignment (default 32); the writer pads every tensor to the
  alignment, so offsets are aligned and non-overlapping.
* expected_bytes = elements / block_elems * block_bytes when elements is a multiple of block_elems.
* the architecture guard accepts iff general.architecture = "qwen4exp" and six hyperparameters
  equal the compiled constants (48, 2560, 512, 10, 24, 2).

## Form template identifiers
block_geometry → `cppGeometry`; BLOCK_GEOMETRY ∘ GGML_TYPES → `pyGeometry`; ggml_type_name →
`cppTypeName`; GGML_TYPES → `pyTypeName`; data_start rounding / writer padding → `alignUp`;
TensorInfo.expected_bytes → `expectedBytes`; check_architecture → `checkArch`; Qwen4ExpGuard →

/-- C++ `block_geometry`: (elements per block, bytes per block). -/

  | 2 => some (32, 18) | 3 => some (32, 20) | 6 => some (32, 22) | 7 => some (32, 24)
  | 8 => some (32, 34) | 9 => some (32, 36)
  | 10 => some (256, 84) | 11 => some (256, 110) | 12 => some (256, 144)
  | 13 => some (256, 176) | 14 => some (256, 210)
  | 16 => some (256, 66) | 17 => some (256, 74) | 18 => some (256, 98)
  | 20 => some (32, 18) | 21 => some (256, 110) | 22 => some (256, 82) | 23 => some (256, 136)
  | 29 => some (256, 56) | 42 => some (64, 18)
  | _ => none

  | 0 => some (1, 4) | 1 => some (1, 2) | 30 => some (1, 2) | 28 => some (1, 8)
  | 2 => some (32, 18) | 3 => some (32, 20) | 6 => some (32, 22) | 7 => some (32, 24)
  | 8 => some (32, 34) | 9 => some (32, 36)
  | 10 => some (256, 84) | 11 => some (256, 110) | 12 => some (256, 144)
  | 13 => some (256, 176) | 14 => some (256, 210) | 15 => some (256, 292)
  | 16 => some (256, 66) | 17 => some (256, 74) | 18 => some (256, 98) | 19 => some (256, 50)
  | 20 => some (32, 18) | 21 => some (256, 110) | 22 => some (256, 82) | 23 => some (256, 136)

  | _ => none

/-- Python `GGML_TYPES` for the same ids. -/

/-- Q2_0 is 64 elements in 18 bytes in both readers. -/

    (List.range 64).all (fun t => (cppGeometry t).isNone || cppGeometry t == pyGeometry t) = true := by
  decide

    cppGeometry 2 = some (32, 2 + 16) ∧            -- Q4_0: d, qs[16]
    cppGeometry 6 = some (32, 2 + 4 + 16) ∧        -- Q5_0: d, qh[4], qs[16]
    cppGeometry 8 = some (32, 2 + 32) ∧            -- Q8_0: d, qs[32]
    cppGeometry 11 = some (256, 32 + 64 + 12 + 2) ∧ -- Q3_K: hmask, qs, scales, d
    cppGeometry 12 = some (256, 2 + 2 + 12 + 128) ∧ -- Q4_K: d, dmin, scales, qs
    cppGeometry 13 = some (256, 2 + 2 + 12 + 32 + 128) ∧ -- Q5_K: d, dmin, scales, qh, qs
    cppGeometry 14 = some (256, 128 + 64 + 16 + 2) ∧ -- Q6_K: ql, qh, scales, d
    cppGeometry 20 = some (32, 2 + 16) ∧           -- IQ4_NL: d, qs[16]
    cppGeometry 23 = some (256, 2 + 2 + 4 + 128) ∧  -- IQ4_XS: d, scales_h, scales_l, qs
    cppGeometry 42 = some (64, 2 + 16) := by        -- Q2_0: d, qs[16]
  decide

  decide

  decide

  unfold alignUp; exact Nat.mul_mod_left _ _

    expectedBytes (k * (per * be)) be bb = k * expectedBytes (per * be) be bb := by
  unfold expectedBytes
  rw [← Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.mul_div_cancel _ hbe, Nat.mul_div_cancel _ hbe, Nat.mul_assoc]

-- § architecture guard

/-- The six required hyperparameters of `Qwen4ExpGuard`. -/
def guardReqs : List (String × Nat) :=
  [("qwen4exp.block_count", 48), ("qwen4exp.embedding_length", 2560),
   ("qwen4exp.expert_count", 512), ("qwen4exp.expert_used_count", 10),
   ("qwen4exp.attention.head_count", 24), ("qwen4exp.attention.head_count_kv", 2)]

/-- `check_architecture`: `none` means accepted, `some msg` is the refusal (only the first

  match arch with
  | none => some "missing general.architecture"
  | some a =>
    if a ≠ "qwen4exp" then some "wrong architecture"
    else guardReqs.foldr (fun r acc =>
      match meta r.1 with
      | none => some ("missing " ++ r.1)
      | some v => if v ≠ r.2 then some r.1 else acc) none

/-- The metadata of the target model. -/
def goodMeta (k : String) : Option Nat := (guardReqs.find? (·.1 == k)).map (·.2)

/-- The target model's metadata is accepted. -/

/-- A different architecture is refused before any hyperparameter is read. -/

    checkArch (some "llama") m = some "wrong architecture" := by
  simp [checkArch]

    checkArch none m = some "missing general.architecture" := rfl

SOURCES: include/strata/artifact/dequant.hpp, tools/canonical_xcheck.py
Integer model of the super-block (256-element) dequantizers Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and IQ4_XS: the
packed 6-bit scale/min unpacking, the walking bit masks, the group/element order, and the code
ranges that decide which canonical form (S4/S8) each type fits.

## Source semantics
* `get_scale_min_k4(j)`: groups 0..3 take 6 bits of q[j] / q[j+4]; groups 4..7 take a nibble of
  q[j+4] and borrow the top two bits of q[j-4] / q[j]. Every scale and min is < 64.

  all eight bits of each qh byte, each used once. Codes are ≤ 31.
* Q6_K: four quads from one qh byte land at strides of 32; the scale index `is + 2*quad` with

* Q3_K: 16 six-bit scales unpacked from 12 bytes (biased by -32); the hmask bit for (half, j) is

  code - 4, i.e. the low bits minus 4 when the mask bit is clear.

get_scale_min_k4 → `scaleMinK4`; unpack_q3_k_scales → `q3Scale`; C++ kmask1/kmask2 repack →
`q3RepackWord`; Q5_K u1/u2 → `q5U1`/`q5U2`; Q6_K is/quad → `q6ScaleIndex`; IQ4_XS ls → `iq4xsLs`;
the 6-bit assembly `lo | (hi << 4)` → `pack6`.
-/

namespace Strata.KQuant

-- § helpers

/-- A disjoint OR is addition: `a | (b << 4) = a + 16 b` when `a < 16`. -/
theorem or_shl4 (a b : Nat) (ha : a < 16) : a ||| (b <<< 4) = a + b * 16 := by
  rw [Nat.or_comm, ← Nat.shiftLeft_add_eq_or_of_lt ha, Nat.shiftLeft_eq]; omega

/-- A nibble mask is `% 16`. -/
theorem and15 (x : Nat) : x &&& 15 = x % 16 := Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod x 4

/-- A 2-bit mask is `% 4`. -/
theorem and3 (x : Nat) : x &&& 3 = x % 4 := Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod x 2

/-- A 6-bit mask is `% 64`. -/
theorem and63 (x : Nat) : x &&& 63 = x % 64 := Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod x 6

/-- Assemble a 6-bit value from a low nibble and a 2-bit high part. -/
def pack6 (lo hi : Nat) : Nat := (lo &&& 15) ||| ((hi &&& 3) <<< 4)

/-- `pack6` is `lo % 16 + 16 * (hi % 4)`, hence always below 64. -/
theorem pack6_eq (lo hi : Nat) : pack6 lo hi = lo % 16 + (hi % 4) * 16 ∧ pack6 lo hi < 64 := by
  unfold pack6
  rw [and15, and3, or_shl4 _ _ (Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide))]
  omega

-- § get_scale_min_k4 (Q4_K, Q5_K)

/-- `get_scale_min_k4(j, q)` returning (scale, min). -/
def scaleMinK4 (j : Nat) (q : Nat → Nat) : Nat × Nat :=
  if j < 4 then (q j &&& 63, q (j + 4) &&& 63)
  else ((q (j + 4) &&& 15) ||| ((q (j - 4) >>> 6) <<< 4),
        (q (j + 4) >>> 4) ||| ((q j >>> 6) <<< 4))

  unfold scaleMinK4

  · simp only [and63]; exact ⟨Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide), Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩
  · have h1 := hq (j + 4); have h2 := hq (j - 4); have h3 := hq j
    simp only [Nat.shiftRight_eq_div_pow]
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [and15, or_shl4 _ _ (Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide))]; omega
    · rw [or_shl4 _ _ (by omega)]; omega

theorem k4_code_byte_lt (e : Nat) (he : e < 256) : 32 * (e / 64) + e % 32 < 128 := by omega

/-- Distinct elements of a 64-element step use distinct (byte, nibble) pairs. -/
theorem k4_address_injective (e f : Nat)
    (hb : 32 * (e / 64) + e % 32 = 32 * (f / 64) + f % 32)
    (hn : (e % 64) / 32 = (f % 64) / 32) : e = f := by omega

def q5U1 (j : Nat) : Nat := 1 <<< (2 * j)
/-- `u2` at step `j` after `j` shifts by two. -/
def q5U2 (j : Nat) : Nat := 2 <<< (2 * j)

theorem q5_masks_cover_byte :

  unfold q6ScaleIndex; omega

theorem q6_code_range (nib hi : Nat) :

  have h := (pack6_eq nib hi).2
  omega

/-- Python `unpack_q3_k_scales`: group `g` (0..15) from the 12 scale bytes `s`. -/
def q3Scale (s : Nat → Nat) (g : Nat) : Nat :=

  let t := s (8 + j)

  have h : q3Scale s g < 64 := by
    unfold q3Scale
    split <;> exact (pack6_eq _ _).2

  let k2 := 0x0f0f0f0f

  | 0 => (a0 &&& k2) ||| (((tmp >>> 0) &&& k1) <<< 4)
  | 1 => (a1 &&& k2) ||| (((tmp >>> 2) &&& k1) <<< 4)
  | 2 => ((a0 >>> 4) &&& k2) ||| (((tmp >>> 4) &&& k1) <<< 4)

    [q3Mask 0 0, q3Mask 0 1, q3Mask 0 2, q3Mask 0 3, q3Mask 1 0, q3Mask 1 1, q3Mask 1 2, q3Mask 1 3] =

      ((c2 + 4 * bit : Nat) : Int) - 4 = (c2 : Int) - (if bit = 1 then 0 else 4) := by

  · split <;> omega

/-!

SOURCES: include/strata/artifact/dequant.hpp, tools/canonical_xcheck.py
Integer model of the super-block (256-element) dequantizers Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and IQ4_XS: the
packed 6-bit scale/min unpacking, the walking bit masks, the group/element order, and the code
ranges that decide which canonical form (S4/S8) each type fits.

## Source semantics
* `get_scale_min_k4(j)`: groups 0..3 take 6 bits of q[j] / q[j+4]; groups 4..7 take a nibble of
  q[j+4] and borrow the top two bits of q[j-4] / q[j]. Every scale and min is < 64.
* Q4_K/Q5_K: each 64-element step emits group `is` (low nibbles) then `is+1` (high nibbles), so
  element e belongs to group e/32.
* Q5_K: `qh` never advances; the 5th bit comes from masks u1 = 1,4,16,64 and u2 = 2,8,32,128, i.e.
  all eight bits of each qh byte, each used once. Codes are ≤ 31.
* Q6_K: four quads from one qh byte land at strides of 32; the scale index `is + 2*quad` with
  is = l/16 equals (position in half)/16. Codes are < 64, biased by -32.
* Q3_K: 16 six-bit scales unpacked from 12 bytes (biased by -32); the hmask bit for (half, j) is
  4*half + j because `m` is never reset; stored code = 2 bits + 4*(hmask bit) ∈ 0..7, decoded as

get_scale_min_k4 → `scaleMinK4`; unpack_q3_k_scales → `q3Scale`; C++ kmask1/kmask2 repack →
`q3RepackWord`; Q5_K u1/u2 → `q5U1`/`q5U2`; Q6_K is/quad → `q6ScaleIndex`; IQ4_XS ls → `iq4xsLs`;

/-- A disjoint OR is addition: `a | (b << 4) = a + 16 b` when `a < 16`. -/

  rw [Nat.or_comm, ← Nat.shiftLeft_add_eq_or_of_lt ha, Nat.shiftLeft_eq]; omega

/-- A nibble mask is `% 16`. -/
theorem and15 (x : Nat) : x &&& 15 = x % 16 := Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod x 4

/-- A 2-bit mask is `% 4`. -/
theorem and3 (x : Nat) : x &&& 3 = x % 4 := Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod x 2

/-- A 6-bit mask is `% 64`. -/
theorem and63 (x : Nat) : x &&& 63 = x % 64 := Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod x 6

/-- Assemble a 6-bit value from a low nibble and a 2-bit high part. -/
def pack6 (lo hi : Nat) : Nat := (lo &&& 15) ||| ((hi &&& 3) <<< 4)

  unfold pack6
  rw [and15, and3, or_shl4 _ _ (Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide))]
  omega

SOURCES: tools/strata_pack.py, tools/canonical_xcheck.py
The canonical-form contract of the pack: one unsigned code per element, packed LSB-first with
`8 / bits` codes per byte (Q2_0's own convention, reused for every form), the MAPPINGS table that
assigns each ggml type its form, group size, code bias and offset plane, and the manifest-driven
decode `value = (code + code_bias) * scale [+ offset]`.

## Source semantics
* `pack_codes` puts code k of each group of `8/bits` at bit offset `k*bits`; `unpack_codes`
  inverts it. For bits = 2 and 4 the round trip is the identity both ways; bits = 8 is a copy.
* Q2_0 → S2 unpacking (`codes[:, t::4]`) and `pack_codes(bits=2)` use the same convention, so
  re-packing a canonical Q2_0 code plane reproduces the source code bytes.
* for every mapping, the largest code the source type can produce fits the form's width, and the
  group size divides the block size (so `elements / group_elems` scales exactly cover a tensor).
* exactly the types with a value-space minimum (Q4_K, Q5_K) carry an offset plane.
* `verify --expert-every N` checks experts 0, N, 2N, … of 512 per layer.

## Form template identifiers
pack_codes → `packByte`; unpack_codes → `unpackByte`; MAPPINGS → `mappings` / `Mapping`;
code_bits(form) → `formBits`; decode_entry's affine branch → `decodeAffine`; choose_scale_dtype →
`chooseScale`; verify_experts sampling → `sampledExperts`.

namespace Strata.Canonical

-- § code packing

/-- Pack `per = 8/bits` codes into one byte, code `k` at bit offset `k*bits` (LSB-first). -/
def packByte (bits : Nat) (cs : List Nat) : Nat :=
  (cs.zipIdx.map fun (c, k) => (c &&& (2 ^ bits - 1)) <<< (k * bits)).foldl (· ||| ·) 0

/-- Unpack `per` codes from one byte. -/
def unpackByte (bits per b : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range per).map fun k => (b >>> (k * bits)) &&& (2 ^ bits - 1)

/-- All lists of `n` codes below `m`. -/
def allCodes (m : Nat) : Nat → List (List Nat)
  | 0 => [[]]
  | n + 1 => (List.range m).flatMap fun c => (allCodes m n).map (c :: ·)

/-- 2-bit codes (S2): every 4-tuple of codes survives pack → unpack. -/
theorem s2_unpack_pack :
    (allCodes 4 4).all (fun cs => unpackByte 2 4 (packByte 2 cs) == cs) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- 2-bit codes (S2): every byte survives unpack → pack, so a re-packed canonical Q2_0 code plane
is byte-identical to the source `qs`. -/
theorem s2_pack_unpack :
    (List.range 256).all (fun b => packByte 2 (unpackByte 2 4 b) == b) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- 4-bit codes (S4): every pair of codes survives pack → unpack. -/
theorem s4_unpack_pack :
    (allCodes 16 2).all (fun cs => unpackByte 4 2 (packByte 4 cs) == cs) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- 4-bit codes (S4): every byte survives unpack → pack. -/
theorem s4_pack_unpack :
    (List.range 256).all (fun b => packByte 4 (unpackByte 4 2 b) == b) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- S2 placement: the code of element `j` lives in byte `j / 4` at bit `2 * (j % 4)` — the Q2_0
source layout and the `t::4` slice describe the same slot. -/
theorem s2_slot (b t : Nat) (ht : t < 4) : (4 * b + t) / 4 = b ∧ 2 * ((4 * b + t) % 4) = t * 2 := by
  omega

-- § mapping table

/-- One MAPPINGS row: (source type, block bytes, block elems, group elems, form bits, code bias,
has offset, non-affine codebook, largest code the source can produce). -/
structure Mapping where
  name : String
  blockBytes : Nat
  blockElems : Nat
  groupElems : Nat
  formBits : Nat
  codeBias : Int
  hasOffset : Bool
  iq4Codebook : Bool
  maxCode : Nat

/-- The quantized rows of MAPPINGS (the P16/P32 rows have no code plane). -/
def mappings : List Mapping :=
  [⟨"Q2_0", 18, 64, 64, 2, -1, false, false, 3⟩,
   ⟨"Q3_K", 110, 256, 16, 4, -4, false, false, 7⟩,
   ⟨"Q4_0", 18, 32, 32, 4, -8, false, false, 15⟩,
   ⟨"Q4_K", 144, 256, 32, 4, 0, true, false, 15⟩,
   ⟨"Q5_0", 22, 32, 32, 8, -16, false, false, 31⟩,
   ⟨"Q5_K", 176, 256, 32, 8, 0, true, false, 31⟩,
   ⟨"Q6_K", 210, 256, 16, 8, -32, false, false, 63⟩,
   ⟨"Q8_0", 34, 32, 32, 8, -128, false, false, 255⟩,
   ⟨"IQ4_NL", 18, 32, 32, 4, 0, false, true, 15⟩,
   ⟨"IQ4_XS", 136, 256, 32, 4, 0, false, true, 15⟩]

/-- Every source code fits the form's width. -/
theorem codes_fit_form : mappings.all (fun m => m.maxCode < 2 ^ m.formBits) = true := by decide

/-- Every group size divides its block size, so scale planes tile tensors exactly. -/
theorem group_divides_block : mappings.all (fun m => m.blockElems % m.groupElems == 0) = true := by
  decide

/-- Exactly Q4_K and Q5_K carry an offset plane (the three-part encoder output). -/
theorem offset_types : (mappings.filter (·.hasOffset)).map (·.name) = ["Q4_K", "Q5_K"] := by decide

/-- Biased types decode symmetric-ish integer ranges: for every affine row the decoded integer
`code + bias` over `0..maxCode` spans `bias .. maxCode + bias`, never above `maxCode`. -/
theorem affine_range :
    (mappings.filter (!·.iq4Codebook)).all
      (fun m => m.codeBias ≤ 0 && (m.maxCode : Int) + m.codeBias ≤ m.maxCode) = true := by decide

/-- The form bit width also packs whole codes into bytes: `8 % bits = 0`. -/
theorem form_bits_pack : mappings.all (fun m => 8 % m.formBits == 0) = true := by decide

-- § decode

/-- The affine branch of `decode_entry` on integers. -/
def decodeAffine (code : Nat) (bias scale offset : Int) : Int := ((code : Int) + bias) * scale + offset

/-- With bias −1 and no offset, the affine decode is exactly Q2_0's `(code − 1) * d`. -/
theorem decode_matches_q2 (c : Nat) (d : Int) : decodeAffine c (-1) d 0 = ((c : Int) - 1) * d := by
  unfold decodeAffine; omega

theorem scales_cover (nBlocks blockElems group : Nat) (hg : 0 < group)
    (hd : blockElems % group = 0) :
    nBlocks * blockElems / group * group = nBlocks * blockElems := by
  have : (nBlocks * blockElems) % group = 0 := by
    rw [Nat.mul_mod, hd, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.zero_mod]
  have h := Nat.div_add_mod (nBlocks * blockElems) group
  rw [this, Nat.add_zero] at h
  rw [Nat.mul_comm]; exact h

/-- `choose_scale_dtype`: keep the 16-bit encoding only when it round-trips. -/
def chooseScale {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] (toHalf : α → α) (x : α) : α × Bool :=
  if toHalf x = x then (toHalf x, true) else (x, false)

/-- Whichever width is chosen, the stored scale equals the original: the choice is never lossy. -/
theorem chooseScale_exact {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] (toHalf : α → α) (x : α) :
    (chooseScale toHalf x).1 = x := by
  unfold chooseScale; split <;> simp_all

-- § expert sampling

/-- Experts visited by `range(0, 512, every)`. -/

/-!
# MODULE: canonical_pack_codes
SOURCES: tools/strata_pack.py, tools/canonical_xcheck.py
The canonical-form contract of the pack: one unsigned code per element, packed LSB-first with
`8 / bits` codes per byte (Q2_0's own convention, reused for every form), the MAPPINGS table that
assigns each ggml type its form, group size, code bias and offset plane, and the manifest-driven
decode `value = (code + code_bias) * scale [+ offset]`.

## Source semantics
* `pack_codes` puts code k of each group of `8/bits` at bit offset `k*bits`; `unpack_codes`
  inverts it. For bits = 2 and 4 the round trip is the identity both ways; bits = 8 is a copy.
* Q2_0 → S2 unpacking (`codes[:, t::4]`) and `pack_codes(bits=2)` use the same convention, so
  re-packing a canonical Q2_0 code plane reproduces the source code bytes.
* for every mapping, the largest code the source type can produce fits the form's width, and the
  group size divides the block size (so `elements / group_elems` scales exactly cover a tensor).
* exactly the types with a value-space minimum (Q4_K, Q5_K) carry an offset plane.
* `verify --expert-every N` checks experts 0, N, 2N, … of 512 per layer.

## Form template identifiers
pack_codes → `packByte`; unpack_codes → `unpackByte`; MAPPINGS → `mappings` / `Mapping`;
code_bits(form) → `formBits`; decode_entry's affine branch → `decodeAffine`; choose_scale_dtype →
`chooseScale`; verify_experts sampling → `sampledExperts`.
-/

namespace Strata.Canonical

-- § code packing

/-- Pack `per = 8/bits` codes into one byte, code `k` at bit offset `k*bits` (LSB-first). -/
def packByte (bits : Nat) (cs : List Nat) : Nat :=
  (cs.zipIdx.map fun (c, k) => (c &&& (2 ^ bits - 1)) <<< (k * bits)).foldl (· ||| ·) 0

/-- Unpack `per` codes from one byte. -/
def unpackByte (bits per b : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range per).map fun k => (b >>> (k * bits)) &&& (2 ^ bits - 1)

/-- All lists of `n` codes below `m`. -/
def allCodes (m : Nat) : Nat → List (List Nat)
  | 0 => [[]]
  | n + 1 => (List.range m).flatMap fun c => (allCodes m n).map (c :: ·)

/-- 2-bit codes (S2): every 4-tuple of codes survives pack → unpack. -/
theorem s2_unpack_pack :
    (allCodes 4 4).all (fun cs => unpackByte 2 4 (packByte 2 cs) == cs) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- 2-bit codes (S2): every byte survives unpack → pack, so a re-packed canonical Q2_0 code plane
is byte-identical to the source `qs`. -/
theorem s2_pack_unpack :
    (List.range 256).all (fun b => packByte 2 (unpackByte 2 4 b) == b) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- 4-bit codes (S4): every pair of codes survives pack → unpack. -/
theorem s4_unpack_pack :
    (allCodes 16 2).all (fun cs => unpackByte 4 2 (packByte 4 cs) == cs) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- 4-bit codes (S4): every byte survives unpack → pack. -/
theorem s4_pack_unpack :
    (List.range 256).all (fun b => packByte 4 (unpackByte 4 2 b) == b) = true := by
  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in decide

/-- S2 placement: the code of element `j` lives in byte `j / 4` at bit `2 * (j % 4)` — the Q2_0
source layout and the `t::4` slice describe the same slot. -/
theorem s2_slot (b t : Nat) (ht : t < 4) : (4 * b + t) / 4 = b ∧ 2 * ((4 * b + t) % 4) = t * 2 := by
  omega

-- § mapping table

/-- One MAPPINGS row: (source type, block bytes, block elems, group elems, form bits, code bias,
has offset, non-affine codebook, largest code the source can produce). -/
structure Mapping where
  name : String
  blockBytes : Nat
  blockElems : Nat
  groupElems : Nat
  formBits : Nat
  codeBias : Int
  hasOffset : Bool
  iq4Codebook : Bool
  maxCode : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- The quantized rows of MAPPINGS (the P16/P32 rows have no code plane). -/
def mappings : List Mapping :=
  [⟨"Q2_0", 18, 64, 64, 2, -1, false, false, 3⟩,
   ⟨"Q3_K", 110, 256, 16, 4, -4, false, false, 7⟩,
   ⟨"Q4_0", 18, 32, 32, 4, -8, false, false, 15⟩,
   ⟨"Q4_K", 144, 256, 32, 4, 0, true, false, 15⟩,
   ⟨"Q5_0", 22, 32, 32, 8, -16, false, false, 31⟩,
   ⟨"Q5_K", 176, 256, 32, 8, 0, true, false, 31⟩,
   ⟨"Q6_K", 210, 256, 16, 8, -32, false, false, 63⟩,
   ⟨"Q8_0", 34, 32, 32, 8, -128, false, false, 255⟩,
   ⟨"IQ4_NL", 18, 32, 32, 4, 0, false, true, 15⟩,
   ⟨"IQ4_XS", 136, 256, 32, 4, 0, false, true, 15⟩]

/-- Every source code fits the form's width. -/
theorem codes_fit_form : mappings.all (fun m => m.maxCode < 2 ^ m.formBits) = true := by decide

/-- Every group size divides its block size, so scale planes tile tensors exactly. -/
theorem group_divides_block : mappings.all (fun m => m.blockElems % m.groupElems == 0) = true := by
  decide

/-- Exactly Q4_K and Q5_K carry an offset plane (the three-part encoder output). -/
theorem offset_types : (mappings.filter (·.hasOffset)).map (·.name) = ["Q4_K", "Q5_K"] := by decide

/-- Biased types decode symmetric-ish integer ranges: for every affine row the decoded integer
`code + bias` over `0..maxCode` spans `bias .. maxCode + bias`, never above `maxCode`. -/
theorem affine_range :
    (mappings.filter (!·.iq4Codebook)).all
      (fun m => m.codeBias ≤ 0 && (m.maxCode : Int) + m.codeBias ≤ m.maxCode) = true := by decide

/-- The form bit width also packs whole codes into bytes: `8 % bits = 0`. -/
theorem form_bits_pack : mappings.all (fun m => 8 % m.formBits == 0) = true := by decide

-- § decode

/-- The affine branch of `decode_entry` on integers. -/
def decodeAffine (code : Nat) (bias scale offset : Int) : Int := ((code : Int) + bias) * scale + offset

/-- With bias −1 and no offset, the affine decode is exactly Q2_0's `(code − 1) * d`. -/
theorem decode_matches_q2 (c : Nat) (d : Int) : decodeAffine c (-1) d 0 = ((c : Int) - 1) * d := by
  unfold decodeAffine; omega

/-- Scale-plane length: `elements / group` scales, exact when elements are whole blocks. -/
theorem scales_cover (nBlocks blockElems group : Nat) (hg : 0 < group)
    (hd : blockElems % group = 0) :
    nBlocks * blockElems / group * group = nBlocks * blockElems := by
  have : (nBlocks * blockElems) % group = 0 := by
    rw [Nat.mul_mod, hd, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.zero_mod]
  have h := Nat.div_add_mod (nBlocks * blockElems) group
  rw [this, Nat.add_zero] at h
  rw [Nat.mul_comm]; exact h

/-- `choose_scale_dtype`: keep the 16-bit encoding only when it round-trips. -/
def chooseScale {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] (toHalf : α → α) (x : α) : α × Bool :=
  if toHalf x = x then (toHalf x, true) else (x, false)

/-- Whichever width is chosen, the stored scale equals the original: the choice is never lossy. -/
theorem chooseScale_exact {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] (toHalf : α → α) (x : α) :
    (chooseScale toHalf x).1 = x := by
  unfold chooseScale; split <;> simp_all

-- § expert sampling

/-- Experts visited by `range(0, 512, every)`. -/
def sampledExperts (every : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range 512).filter fun e => e % every == 0

/-- The default `--expert-every 32` checks 16 experts per layer, starting at expert 0. -/
theorem default_sampling : (sampledExperts 32).length = 16 ∧ (sampledExperts 32).head? = some 0 := by
  decide

end Strata.Canonical

  constructor
  · omega
  · intro h; omega

    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this; exact this

    48 * nExperts * blobBytes = 33973862400 ∧
      3164 * 2 ^ 30 ≤ 100 * 33973862400 ∧ 100 * 33973862400 < 3165 * 2 ^ 30 := by decide

    offDCodes = 819200 ∧ offGuScales = 1228800 ∧ offDScales = 1331200 ∧
      offDScales + hDim * 10 * 2 = blobBytes := by decide

/-- Interleaved gate/up row slot: role 0 = gate, 1 = up. -/
def guSlot (row role : Nat) : Nat := 2 * row + role

/-- Code offset of block `blk` of a gate/up role. -/

/-- Scale offset of block `blk` of a gate/up role. -/
def guScaleOff (role blk : Nat) : Nat := offGuScales + (guSlot (blk / 40) role * 40 + blk % 40) * 2
/-- Code offset of block `blk` of the down role. -/
def dCodeOff (blk : Nat) : Nat := offDCodes + blk / 10 * 160 + blk % 10 * 16
/-- Scale offset of block `blk` of the down role. -/
def dScaleOff (blk : Nat) : Nat := offDScales + (blk / 10 * 10 + blk % 10) * 2

/-- Blocks per role per expert. -/
theorem blocks_per_role : hDim * ffDim / qk = 25600 ∧ 25600 * blockBytes = roleBytes := by decide

  omega

    guCodeOff role blk + 16 ≤ offDCodes := by
  unfold guCodeOff guSlot offGuCodes offDCodes ffDim; omega

  unfold guCodeOff guSlot offGuCodes at h; omega

  unfold guScaleOff guSlot offGuScales offDScales offDCodes offGuCodes ffDim hDim
  constructor
  · omega
  · intro h; omega

    (offDCodes ≤ dCodeOff b1 ∧ dCodeOff b1 + 16 ≤ offGuScales) ∧
      (dCodeOff b1 = dCodeOff b2 → b1 = b2) := by
  unfold dCodeOff offDCodes offGuScales offGuCodes ffDim hDim
  constructor
  · omega
  · intro h; omega

theorem d_scale_in_plane_injective (b1 b2 : Nat) (hb1 : b1 < 25600) :
    (offDScales ≤ dScaleOff b1 ∧ dScaleOff b1 + 2 ≤ blobBytes) ∧
      (dScaleOff b1 = dScaleOff b2 → b1 = b2) := by
  unfold dScaleOff offDScales offGuScales offDCodes offGuCodes ffDim hDim blobBytes roleBytes
    qk blockBytes
  constructor
  · omega
  · intro h; omega

theorem slot_counts :
    2 * 25600 * 16 = offDCodes - offGuCodes ∧ 25600 * 16 = offGuScales - offDCodes ∧
      2 * 25600 * 2 = offDScales - offGuScales ∧ 25600 * 2 = blobBytes - offDScales := by decide

/-- Start of blob (layer, expert) in `experts.bin`. -/

    (h : (l1, e1) ≠ (l2, e2)) :
    blobStart l1 e1 + blobBytes ≤ blobStart l2 e2 ∨ blobStart l2 e2 + blobBytes ≤ blobStart l1 e1 := by
  unfold blobStart nExperts blobBytes roleBytes hDim ffDim blockBytes qk
  simp only [ne_eq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  have : l1 * 512 + e1 ≠ l2 * 512 + e2 := by omega
  rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne this with hlt | hgt
  · left
    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (2560 * 640 * 18 / 64 * 3) (show l1 * 512 + e1 + 1 ≤ l2 * 512 + e2 by omega)
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this; exact this
  · right
    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (2560 * 640 * 18 / 64 * 3) (show l2 * 512 + e2 + 1 ≤ l1 * 512 + e1 by omega)
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this; exact this

theorem expert_runs_tile : nExperts * roleBytes = hDim * ffDim * nExperts * blockBytes / qk := by
  decide

theorem arena_size :
    48 * nExperts * blobBytes = 33973862400 ∧
      3164 * 2 ^ 30 ≤ 100 * 33973862400 ∧ 100 * 33973862400 < 3165 * 2 ^ 30 := by decide

SOURCES: tools/pack_index.py
The flat engine index derived from the pack manifest: per-tensor load KIND, the three engine-form
plane sizes (codes, scales widened to f32, offsets), the consistency checks between pack-form and
engine-form widths, the aligned engine pool, and the activation-type column.

  (real RNE narrowing, 2 B/elem); F16 stored as fp16 → VERBATIM; F32 → F32 copy; quantized →
  VERBATIM planes.
* engine scales are ALWAYS 4 bytes; pack scales are 2 bytes when `scales_fp16`. Hence
  dst_bytes = src_bytes + widening, widening = ne1·n_groups·2 exactly when scales are fp16.
* the planes must be contiguous in the order codes, scales, offsets and fill the span exactly.
* engine offsets: dst advances by `align_up(dst + dst_bytes)`, so every tensor starts aligned and
  tensors never overlap.
* act_kind (Q8_0 vs Q8_K activations) cannot be recovered from the S-form fields: IQ4_NL and
  IQ4_XS share every S-form field yet differ in act_kind.
* the written row has 19 columns (including act_kind); the module docstring lists only 18.

## Form template identifiers
kind selection → `loadKind`; plane sizes → `enginePlanes`/`packPlanes`; widening → `widening`;
align_up → `alignUp`; VDT → `actKind`; S-form fields → `SForm`/`sform`; header columns →
`headerColumns`/`docColumns`.
-/

namespace Strata.PackIndex

-- § load kind

/-- The four load kinds of the index. -/
inductive Kind | verbatim | bf16InF32 | f32Copy | f16InF32
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- `kind` from `source_type` and `values_fp16`, in the script's branch order. -/
def loadKind (st : String) (valuesFp16 : Bool) : Kind :=
  if st = "BF16" then .bf16InF32
  else if st = "F16" ∧ !valuesFp16 then .f16InF32
  else if st = "F16" then .verbatim
  else if st = "F32" then .f32Copy
  else .verbatim

/-- Engine bytes for the float kinds. -/
def floatDst (k : Kind) (elems srcBytes : Nat) : Nat :=
  match k with
  | .bf16InF32 => elems * 2
  | .f16InF32 => elems * 2
  | .f32Copy => elems * 4
  | .verbatim => srcBytes

/-- The two 16-bit source types are re-rounded to 2 bytes per element whenever the pack promoted
them, and the promoted pack holds 4 bytes per element, so the saving is exactly half. -/
theorem rerounding_halves (elems : Nat) :
    floatDst (loadKind "BF16" false) elems (elems * 4) = elems * 2 ∧
      floatDst (loadKind "F16" false) elems (elems * 4) = elems * 2 ∧
      elems * 4 - elems * 2 = elems * 2 := by
  simp [loadKind, floatDst]; omega

/-- An F16 tensor already stored as fp16 is copied verbatim. -/
theorem f16_kept_verbatim (elems : Nat) :
    loadKind "F16" true = .verbatim ∧ floatDst (loadKind "F16" true) elems (elems * 2) = elems * 2 := by
  simp [loadKind, floatDst]

/-- Quantized types always load verbatim (their planes are re-sized, not re-encoded). -/
theorem quantized_verbatim : loadKind "Q2_0" false = .verbatim ∧ loadKind "Q4_K" true = .verbatim := by
  simp [loadKind]

-- § plane sizes

/-- Pack-form plane bytes: scales/offsets are 2 B if their fp16 flag is set, else 4 B. -/
def packPlanes (codes groups : Nat) (scFp16 hasOff offFp16 : Bool) : Nat :=
  codes + groups * (if scFp16 then 2 else 4) + (if hasOff then groups * (if offFp16 then 2 else 4) else 0)

/-- Engine-form plane bytes: scales and offsets are always 4 B. -/
def enginePlanes (codes groups : Nat) (hasOff : Bool) : Nat :=
  codes + groups * 4 + (if hasOff then groups * 4 else 0)

/-- Widening cost of a tensor: the extra 2 B per scale when the pack holds fp16 scales. -/
def widening (groups : Nat) (scFp16 : Bool) : Nat := if scFp16 then groups * 4 - groups * 2 else 0

/-- The check `dst_bytes == src_bytes + widen_here` holds whenever offsets are f32 (true for all
54 offset-carrying tensors of the current pack). -/
theorem engine_eq_pack_plus_widening (codes groups : Nat) (scFp16 hasOff : Bool) :
    enginePlanes codes groups hasOff =
      packPlanes codes groups scFp16 hasOff false + widening groups scFp16 := by
  unfold enginePlanes packPlanes widening
  cases scFp16 <;> cases hasOff <;> simp <;> omega

/-- If a future pack had fp16 OFFSETS, the same check would refuse it (widening counts scales
only), which is the conservative outcome. -/
theorem fp16_offsets_detected (codes groups : Nat) (hg : 0 < groups) :
    enginePlanes codes groups true ≠ packPlanes codes groups false true true + widening groups false := by
  unfold enginePlanes packPlanes widening; simp; omega

/-- Engine planes are never smaller than pack planes. -/
theorem engine_ge_pack (codes groups : Nat) (scFp16 hasOff offFp16 : Bool) :
    packPlanes codes groups scFp16 hasOff offFp16 ≤ enginePlanes codes groups hasOff := by
  unfold enginePlanes packPlanes
  cases scFp16 <;> cases hasOff <;> cases offFp16 <;> simp <;> omega

/-- Number of scale groups: `ne1 * (ne0 / group)`, and codes are `elems * bits / 8` bytes. -/
theorem groups_cover (ne0 ne1 g : Nat) (hd : ne0 % g = 0) : ne1 * (ne0 / g) * g = ne1 * ne0 := by
  rw [Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.div_mul_cancel (Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero hd)]

-- § contiguity

/-- Planes laid out contiguously in key order fill `[off, off + codes + scales + offsets)`. -/
theorem contiguous_span (off c s o : Nat) :
    let codesOff := off
    let scalesOff := codesOff + c
    let offsOff := scalesOff + s
    offsOff + o - off = c + s + o := by
  simp only; omega

-- § engine pool

/-- `align_up`. -/
def alignUp (n a : Nat) : Nat := (n + a - 1) / a * a

/-- The next destination offset is aligned and leaves room for the current tensor. -/
theorem next_dst (dst bytes : Nat) :
    dst + bytes ≤ alignUp (dst + bytes) 64 ∧ alignUp (dst + bytes) 64 % 64 = 0 := by
  unfold alignUp; omega

-- § activation kind

/-- The activation each weight type wants (VDT): 0 = Q8_0, 1 = Q8_K. -/
def actKind : String → Nat
  | "Q3_K" | "Q4_K" | "Q5_K" | "Q6_K" | "IQ4_XS" => 1
  | _ => 0

/-- The S-form fields the engine sees: (code bits, code bias, IQ4 codebook, has offset). -/
structure SForm where
  bits : Nat
  bias : Int
  iq4 : Bool
  offset : Bool
deriving DecidableEq

/-- S-form fields per type, from the MAPPINGS table. -/
def sform : String → SForm
  | "IQ4_NL" => ⟨4, 0, true, false⟩
  | "IQ4_XS" => ⟨4, 0, true, false⟩
  | "Q5_0" => ⟨8, -16, false, false⟩
  | "Q5_K" => ⟨8, 0, false, true⟩
  | _ => ⟨0, 0, false, false⟩

/-- IQ4_NL and IQ4_XS agree on every S-form field yet need different activations: act_kind must
be carried in the index. -/
theorem act_kind_not_derivable : sform "IQ4_NL" = sform "IQ4_XS" ∧ actKind "IQ4_NL" ≠ actKind "IQ4_XS" := by
  decide

/-- The source comment says Q5_0 and Q5_K differ only in `has_offset`; per MAPPINGS their code
bias differs too (-16 vs 0). Both differ in act_kind either way. -/
theorem q5_forms_differ_in_bias :
    (sform "Q5_0").bias ≠ (sform "Q5_K").bias ∧ (sform "Q5_0").offset ≠ (sform "Q5_K").offset ∧
      actKind "Q5_0" ≠ actKind "Q5_K" := by decide

-- § index format

/-- Columns written by the header line and the row format string. -/
def headerColumns : List String :=
  ["name", "file", "kind", "src_off", "src_bytes", "dst_off", "dst_bytes", "ne0", "ne1",
   "code_bits", "code_bias", "group_elems", "codebook", "has_offset", "codes_bytes",
   "scales_bytes", "offset_bytes", "scales_fp16", "act_kind"]

/-- Columns listed in the module docstring. -/
def docColumns : List String := headerColumns.take 18

/-- The row has 19 fields; the docstring documents 18 and omits act_kind. -/
theorem column_counts : headerColumns.length = 19 ∧ docColumns.length = 18 ∧
    headerColumns.getLast? = some "act_kind" := by decide

/-- The reported widening cost, 11,407,360 B, is 10.88 MiB. -/
theorem widening_mib : 1087 * 2 ^ 20 ≤ 100 * 11407360 ∧ 100 * 11407360 < 1088 * 2 ^ 20 := by decide

end Strata.PackIndex

    floatDst (loadKind "BF16" false) elems (elems * 4) = elems * 2 ∧
      floatDst (loadKind "F16" false) elems (elems * 4) = elems * 2 ∧
      elems * 4 - elems * 2 = elems * 2 := by
  simp [loadKind, floatDst]; omega

/-- An F16 tensor already stored as fp16 is copied verbatim. -/
theorem f16_kept_verbatim (elems : Nat) :
    loadKind "F16" true = .verbatim ∧ floatDst (loadKind "F16" true) elems (elems * 2) = elems * 2 := by
  simp [loadKind, floatDst]

/-- Quantized types always load verbatim (their planes are re-sized, not re-encoded). -/
theorem quantized_verbatim : loadKind "Q2_0" false = .verbatim ∧ loadKind "Q4_K" true = .verbatim := by
  simp [loadKind]

-- § plane sizes

/-- Pack-form plane bytes: scales/offsets are 2 B if their fp16 flag is set, else 4 B. -/
def packPlanes (codes groups : Nat) (scFp16 hasOff offFp16 : Bool) : Nat :=
  codes + groups * (if scFp16 then 2 else 4) + (if hasOff then groups * (if offFp16 then 2 else 4) else 0)

/-- Engine-form plane bytes: scales and offsets are always 4 B. -/
def enginePlanes (codes groups : Nat) (hasOff : Bool) : Nat :=
  codes + groups * 4 + (if hasOff then groups * 4 else 0)

/-- Widening cost of a tensor: the extra 2 B per scale when the pack holds fp16 scales. -/
def widening (groups : Nat) (scFp16 : Bool) : Nat := if scFp16 then groups * 4 - groups * 2 else 0

/-- The check `dst_bytes == src_bytes + widen_here` holds whenever offsets are f32 (true for all
54 offset-carrying tensors of the current pack). -/
theorem engine_eq_pack_plus_widening (codes groups : Nat) (scFp16 hasOff : Bool) :
    enginePlanes codes groups hasOff =
      packPlanes codes groups scFp16 hasOff false + widening groups scFp16 := by
  unfold enginePlanes packPlanes widening
  cases scFp16 <;> cases hasOff <;> simp <;> omega

/-- If a future pack had fp16 OFFSETS, the same check would refuse it (widening counts scales
only), which is the conservative outcome. -/
theorem fp16_offsets_detected (codes groups : Nat) (hg : 0 < groups) :
    enginePlanes codes groups true ≠ packPlanes codes groups false true true + widening groups false := by
  unfold enginePlanes packPlanes widening; simp; omega

/-- Engine planes are never smaller than pack planes. -/
theorem engine_ge_pack (codes groups : Nat) (scFp16 hasOff offFp16 : Bool) :
    packPlanes codes groups scFp16 hasOff offFp16 ≤ enginePlanes codes groups hasOff := by
  unfold enginePlanes packPlanes
  cases scFp16 <;> cases hasOff <;> cases offFp16 <;> simp <;> omega

/-- Number of scale groups: `ne1 * (ne0 / group)`, and codes are `elems * bits / 8` bytes. -/
theorem groups_cover (ne0 ne1 g : Nat) (hd : ne0 % g = 0) : ne1 * (ne0 / g) * g = ne1 * ne0 := by
  rw [Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.div_mul_cancel (Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero hd)]

-- § contiguity

/-- Planes laid out contiguously in key order fill `[off, off + codes + scales + offsets)`. -/
theorem contiguous_span (off c s o : Nat) :
    let codesOff := off
    let scalesOff := codesOff + c
    let offsOff := scalesOff + s
    offsOff + o - off = c + s + o := by
  simp only; omega

-- § engine pool

/-- `align_up`. -/
def alignUp (n a : Nat) : Nat := (n + a - 1) / a * a

/-- The next destination offset is aligned and leaves room for the current tensor. -/
theorem next_dst (dst bytes : Nat) :
    dst + bytes ≤ alignUp (dst + bytes) 64 ∧ alignUp (dst + bytes) 64 % 64 = 0 := by
  unfold alignUp; omega

-- § activation kind

/-- The activation each weight type wants (VDT): 0 = Q8_0, 1 = Q8_K. -/
def actKind : String → Nat
  | "Q3_K" | "Q4_K" | "Q5_K" | "Q6_K" | "IQ4_XS" => 1
  | _ => 0

/-- The S-form fields the engine sees: (code bits, code bias, IQ4 codebook, has offset). -/
structure SForm where
  bits : Nat
  bias : Int
  iq4 : Bool
  offset : Bool
deriving DecidableEq

/-- S-form fields per type, from the MAPPINGS table. -/
def sform : String → SForm
  | "IQ4_NL" => ⟨4, 0, true, false⟩
  | "IQ4_XS" => ⟨4, 0, true, false⟩
  | "Q5_0" => ⟨8, -16, false, false⟩
  | "Q5_K" => ⟨8, 0, false, true⟩
  | _ => ⟨0, 0, false, false⟩

/-- IQ4_NL and IQ4_XS agree on every S-form field yet need different activations: act_kind must
be carried in the index. -/
theorem act_kind_not_derivable : sform "IQ4_NL" = sform "IQ4_XS" ∧ actKind "IQ4_NL" ≠ actKind "IQ4_XS" := by
  decide

/-- The source comment says Q5_0 and Q5_K differ only in `has_offset`; per MAPPINGS their code
bias differs too (-16 vs 0). Both differ in act_kind either way. -/
theorem q5_forms_differ_in_bias :
    (sform "Q5_0").bias ≠ (sform "Q5_K").bias ∧ (sform "Q5_0").offset ≠ (sform "Q5_K").offset ∧
      actKind "Q5_0" ≠ actKind "Q5_K" := by decide

-- § index format

/-- Columns written by the header line and the row format string. -/
def headerColumns : List String :=
  ["name", "file", "kind", "src_off", "src_bytes", "dst_off", "dst_bytes", "ne0", "ne1",
   "code_bits", "code_bias", "group_elems", "codebook", "has_offset", "codes_bytes",
   "scales_bytes", "offset_bytes", "scales_fp16", "act_kind"]

/-- Columns listed in the module docstring. -/
def docColumns : List String := headerColumns.take 18

/-- The row has 19 fields; the docstring documents 18 and omits act_kind. -/
theorem column_counts : headerColumns.length = 19 ∧ docColumns.length = 18 ∧
    headerColumns.getLast? = some "act_kind" := by decide

/-- The reported widening cost, 11,407,360 B, is 10.88 MiB. -/
theorem widening_mib : 1087 * 2 ^ 20 ≤ 100 * 11407360 ∧ 100 * 11407360 < 1088 * 2 ^ 20 := by decide

end Strata.PackIndex

I wrote 9 Lean modules with 139 theorems covering all 10 assigned files. All of them check with no errors, no `sorry` and no `native_decide`.

**How they were checked.** I could not use Axle: `axle.axiommath.ai` was unreachable from my environment (HTTP 000), and the session cookie and CSRF values were placeholders anyway. Instead I downloaded the official Lean 4.20.0 release from GitHub and checked every file with it. The files use only core Lean (no imports), so they should also work under Axle's `ignore_imports`, but they have not been run on lean-4.35.0.

The tools ran in my own sandbox; I saw no sign of a mirrored machine. I didn't use any credentials. The `/tmp/ref_Niko1221_Strata.git` repo was not present, so I worked only from the source given in the task.

**Modules:**
- **Q2BlockCodebook** covers the Q2_0 block: how each element's 2-bit code is located, the `{-1,0,+1,+2}` value set, and the writer's quantizer. One finding: re-quantizing dequantized values only gives back the same codes if no code is 3. A proven counterexample shows code 3 coming back as 2.
- **Fp16BitConversion** models both fp16 directions bit-exactly. It proves fp16 → f32 → fp16 returns every normal fp16 unchanged, and checks the source's test values. It also confirms the earlier version's bug: it turned the finite value 1e30 into NaN instead of infinity.
- **Bf16BitConversion** proves the round-down, round-up and round-to-even cases, and that bf16 → f32 → bf16 returns all 65,536 patterns unchanged. It also shows the "bit 15" variant goes wrong only on exact ties.
- **GgufHeaderLayout** proves the C++ block-size table agrees with Python wherever C++ defines a size, and that each block's byte count is the sum of its fields. It also covers the file magic, alignment and the architecture check. It records two table inconsistencies: Python's id 41 duplicates id 33's name, and C++ has no name for id 29.
- **KQuantScaleUnpacking** covers how the 6-bit scales are unpacked and how elements are ordered within blocks, for Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and IQ4_XS. The C++ and Python Q3_K scale unpacking are compared on test inputs only, not proved equal in general.
- **LegacyBlockLayouts** covers Q4_0, Q5_0, Q8_0 and IQ4_NL. It proves the source's Q5_0 high-bit expression equals the simpler form the canonicaliser uses. It also proves the Q8_0 +128 storage round-trips exactly, and that the IQ4_NL value table is sorted but not evenly spaced.
- **CanonicalPackCodes** proves code packing and unpacking round-trip for every possible input at 2 and 4 bits. Over the mapping table, it proves every type's codes fit its storage width and every scale group divides its block.
- **ExpertBlobLayout** proves the 1,382,400-byte expert blob layout puts every block in its own slot inside the right section. It also proves different blobs never overlap and the full arena is 31.64 GiB.
- **PackIndexPlanes** proves the engine size equals the pack size plus the fp16-scale widening, and that IQ4_NL and IQ4_XS can't be told apart without the extra activation column. Two documentation mismatches:
  - The source comment says Q5_0 and Q5_K differ only in offset, but their code bias differs too.
  - The docstring lists 18 columns, but each row has 19.
